items.title: Three men nabbed in cable theft attempt in Taman Seri Sentosa
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Three men were arrested after police found them inside a utility manhole during an operation to investigate an attempted cable theft in Taman Seri Sentosa here yesterday. Brickfields police chief Assistant Commissioner Hoo Chang Hook said the operation began at 4pm after police received public information about suspicious activities at the location. "A team from the Petaling police station task force, assisted by other police personnel, inspected the location and found two men inside the utility manhole.

items.title: Make health insurance mandatory for UNHCR-registered refugees, govt urged
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The government should require all refugees registered with the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR) to have health insurance, to ease the financial burden on public healthcare facilities. Datuk Dr Mohd Radzi Md Jidin (PN-Putrajaya) said UNHCR should take responsibility for refugees issued with its cards by ensuring they were insured when seeking treatment at government hospitals and clinics. He said the increase of 7,907 occurred despite the Cabinet's July 23 directive for UNHCR to temporarily stop registering new refugees.

items.title: Trump, Thai PM to announce trade progress, not final deal
items.summary: BANGKOK: US President Donald Trump will sign a joint statement with Thailand's premier on Tuesday marking "significant progress" in trade negotiations, but will not ink a final deal, a Thai official said. A framework agreement was unveiled just over a year ago, on the same day as Trump announced a short-lived ceasefire between Thailand and its neighbour Cambodia following deadly border clashes. The United States is Thailand's largest export market, with the Southeast Asian nation recording a surplus of US$71.7 billion last year, according to US data.

items.title: News@9: Today's top headlines - November 17, 2026 [WATCH]
items.summary: Here are today's biggest stories: French investment sought Malaysia is seeking greater French investment, particularly in rare earth processing, as both countries look to deepen economic ties and expand cooperation in strategic sectors. Macron visits Petaling Street Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim took Emmanuel Macron on an informal visit to Petaling Street during the French president's official visit to Malaysia. Ismail resigned voluntarily Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said Umno did not instruct Ismail Lasim to resign as Negri Sembilan Menteri Besar, adding that the decision was made voluntarily.

items.title: SC unveils Sukuk Prisma for climate adaption and resilience
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Securities Commission Malaysia (SC) today introduced Sukuk Prisma to the global market, a new purpose-driven sustainable sukuk framework designed to mobilise capital for climate adaptation and resilience, supporting wider sustainable development priorities. In a statement, the SC said the framework expands the capital market's scope beyond conventional green and social categories to encompass broader climate adaptation, resilience and transitional financing, including flood mitigation, coastal protection, agriculture and the resilience of power grids. The SC will issue the Sukuk Prisma Framework in the first quarter of 2027.

items.title: PEOPLElogy’s leaders conference rallies corporate Malaysia to put people first in AI push, as ex-HRD Corp chief warns against cutting training
items.summary: PETALING JAYA, Nov 17 — Corporate Malaysia must keep investing in its people to get real value from artificial intelligence (AI), Green Packet Bhd managing director and group chief executive officer Datuk Shahul Hameed Shaik Dawood said as PEOPLElogy Berhad opened its Build a Future Team (BAFT) Leaders Conference 2026 today. PEOPLElogy founder and managing director Allen Lee said: “Datuk Shahul has said what every leader in this room needs to hear. “Being AI ready is not about being technical.

items.title: 25 foreign women detained in Changkat prostitution crackdown
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Immigration officers detained 25 foreign women, including 14 from African countries, during a crackdown on suspected prostitution activities targeting tourists and foreign workers in Changkat, Bukit Bintang, early today. Kuala Lumpur Immigration director Datuk Hamsha Injau said the operation, codenamed Ops Gegar, was the third conducted at the same location this year to curb prostitution and other illegal activities involving foreigners. Hamsha said all 25 women inspected were detained for various immigration offences.

items.title: Malaysia approves RM812.68mil in digital investments from France between 2024 and 2026
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia approved RM812.68 million in digital investments from France between 2024 and 2026, making the country the fifth-largest European source of such investments over the period. Digital Minister Gobind Singh Deo said Malaysia wants to build on those investments by encouraging French companies to develop and commercialise new technologies with Malaysian businesses, universities and research institutions, and use the country as a base to serve the wider Asean market. Among the French companies with Malaysia Digital status are AXA Group Operations Malaysia, CACEIS Malaysia of the Crédit Agricole Group, Sanofi-Aventis (Malaysia), Orange Business Services Malaysia, Schneider Electric IT Malaysia and CMA CGM Group.

items.title: Trump takes reported Iran dirty bomb threat to Washington 'very seriously'
items.summary: MANILA: President Donald Trump said Tuesday that US authorities take "very seriously" any possible threat to Washington, following reports Iran was planning to target officials, possibly with a radioactive bomb. CNN, citing seven anonymous US officials, reported that US intelligence indicated that Iran was preparing to target senior Trump administration officials by detonating a so-called dirty bomb in Washington. Iran's foreign ministry spokesman Esmaeil Baqaei dismissed the report as "fabricated", suggesting Washington was "seeking to lay the media groundwork for their sinister designs."

items.title: Citaglobal completes acquisition of 70pct stake in Perak hydropower assets
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Citaglobal Bhd's subsidiary, Citaglobal Renewable Energy Sdn Bhd, has completed the acquisition of 70 per cent equity interests in Zeqna Corporation Sdn Bhd and Koridor Mentari Sdn Bhd, giving the group controlling stakes in two hydropower assets in Perak. Zeqna owns the Slim hydropower plant, while Koridor Mentari holds the Kampar hydropower project. With the Slim hydropower plant already generating recurring revenue, the group's new energy business is building a sustainable income stream while advancing its pipeline of larger-scale energy projects, Citaglobal said.

items.title: Malaysian OGSE firms generate RM114.82mil in export sales as at Sept 30
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: A total of 77 Malaysian Oil and Gas Services and Equipment (OGSE) companies have generated RM114.82 million in export sales as at Sept 30 this year, said Economy Minister Akmal Nasrullah Mohd Nasir. He said the export sales were an achievement, through export promotion and international business development programmes facilitated by the Malaysia External Trade Development Corporation, reflecting progress under the National OGSE Industry Blueprint 2021-2030. "Through the OGSE Finance Centre of Excellence, 27 companies secured RM125 million in financing approvals, while six projects under the OGSE Catalyst Programme have been commercialised, generating RM10.1 million in sales.

items.title: Anwar orders immediate aid for family of policeman killed in Sungkai crash
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed immediate assistance to be provided to the family of a policeman killed in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, today, as well as to other officers injured in the incident. "My condolences to the family of the late Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob, a police officer who lost his life in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, today. "May his family be granted strength and fortitude in facing this loss, and may the injured police officers have a speedy recovery.

items.title: Malaysian palm oil industry well-positioned for EUDR compliance – MPOB
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Malaysia's oil palm industry is well-positioned to meet the requirements of the European Union Deforestation Regulation (EUDR), backed by a longstanding sustainability framework, mandatory national certification and ongoing efforts to strengthen digital traceability across the supply chain. The Malaysian Palm Oil Board (MPOB) in a statement said Malaysia is moving beyond sustainability commitments towards a system that could demonstrate, through verifiable information, where its palm oil comes from, how it is produced and how it moves through the supply chain. The MPOB noted that the Malaysian Sustainable Palm Oil (MSPO) certification scheme was introduced in 2013, with implementation commencing in 2015, reflecting the country's recognition that responsible production and environmental stewardship are fundamental to the industry's long-term competitiveness.

items.title: Police seek dashcam footage of fatal Penang crash
items.summary: Northeast district police chief Assistant Commissioner Abdul Rozak Muhammad said investigators were piecing together the circumstances surrounding the 1pm accident along Jalan Lembah Permai. He said initial investigations found that the 36-year-old motorcyclist was heading home to Batu Ferringhi from Penang Hospital with her daughter when she lost control of her motorcycle. Abdul Rozak said the motorcyclist was pronounced dead at the scene, while her daughter sustained chest injuries and was taken back to Penang Hospital for treatment.

items.title: Tuanku Muhriz grants Ismail audience amid Negri Sembilan constitutional crisis
items.summary: SEREMBAN: The Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negri Sembilan, Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir, granted an audience today to Menteri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim following the current political impasse affecting the state. Earlier this morning, the Negri Sembilan Palace said the menteri besar's resignation would only take effect upon receiving the consent of Tuanku Muhriz, in accordance with the provisions of the Negri Sembilan state constitution. Ismail was sworn in as Negri Sembilan menteri besar on Aug 2.

items.title: GTA Holdings, France's Safran team up on helicopter engine maintenance
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: GTA Holdings Bhd has teamed up with France's Safran Group to develop helicopter engine repair and training capabilities in Malaysia. This follows a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) signed by their respective subsidiaries, Global Turbine Asia Sdn Bhd and Safran Helicopter Engines Asia Pte Ltd. GTA said the proposed cooperation could help it secure higher-value maintenance, repair and overhaul (MRO) opportunities, including potential demand from the Royal Malaysian Air Force's (RMAF) proposed acquisition of four additional Airbus helicopters. GTA said the proposed fleet expansion could generate additional MRO opportunities over the lifespan of the new engines.

items.title: Autistic girl, 6, fighting for life after Penang crash kills mother
items.summary: The deceased's younger brother, Muhammad Firdaus Muhammad Lizan, 32, said his sister, Amira Mohd Lizan, 36, had earlier finished selling nasi lemak and kuih with their mother before taking her youngest daughter to the hospital. They had actually just returned from the hospital," he said when met at the Penang Hospital mortuary. Firdaus said Seroja Dania remained in critical condition at the hospital's emergency unit, dispelling earlier rumours in their village that both mother and daughter had died.

items.title: Firemen rescue 16 people aged 65 to 85, after flash floods hit Kluang nursing home
items.summary: KLUANG, Nov 17 — Firemen rescued 16 elderly residents from a nursing home hit by flash floods following a downpour in Jalan Haji Manan here today. In a press statement, Kluang Fire and Rescue Station operations commander Fadly A. Karim said the station received an emergency call at 5.11pm. Firefighters help evacuate 16 people from a flooded nursing home on Jalan Haji Manan in Kluang, November 17, 2026.

items.title: Health Ministry has only 19 cardiothoracic surgeons
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Only 19 cardiothoracic surgeons are currently serving at six of the seven Health Ministry hospitals offering heart surgery. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said 37 medical officers were undergoing specialist training, comprising four under Universiti Teknologi Mara's Master of Surgery programme and 33 through the parallel pathway. Yunus cited the resignation of the ministry's head of cardiothoracic surgery services, Dr Basheer Ahamed Abdul Kareem, on Oct 23.

items.title: Policeman whose wrist was severed in Kepong machete attack considered for field promotion
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A policeman whose right wrist was severed in a machete attack by a foreign man in Desa Aman Puri, Kepong, on November 11 is being considered for a field promotion. Bukit Aman Crime Prevention and Community Safety Department (JPJKK) director Datuk Noor Hisam Nordin said Inspector-General of Police Tan Sri Mohd Khalid Ismail had proposed the promotion in recognition of the officer’s dedication to duty. Also present were Deputy Inspector-General of Police Datuk Seri Abdul Aziz Abdul Majid, Bukit Aman JPJKK Deputy Directors Datuk Suryani Sungit and Datuk Nik Ros Azhan Nik Ab Hamid, and Selangor JPJKK chief Senior Assistant Commissioner Mohamad Fakhrudin Abdul Hamid.

items.title: Shah Alam Line resumes normal operations after tree falls on tracks [WATCH]
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Rapid KL's Shah Alam Line has resumed normal operations after a fallen tree disrupted train services near UiTM Shah Alam station earlier today. In a statement, Rapid KL said the tree fell onto the tracks following bad weather at 5.22pm, forcing services to be suspended for more than an hour. Normal operations resumed at 6.43pm.

items.title: Two women lose RM1.18m to phone scammers posing as police
items.summary: BATU PAHAT, Nov 17 — Two women in Batu Pahat and Kuala Terengganu suffered combined losses of over RM1.18 million after being duped by phone scammers posing as police officers. In Batu Pahat, a secondary school teacher suffered losses amounting to RM748,326.50 after falling victim to a phone scam involving a suspect posing as a Bukit Aman police officer. Shahrulanuar said the victim checked her bank account last week and discovered several money transfers totalling RM673,326.50 to accounts belonging to unknown individuals.

items.title: Bangladeshi worker killed in Kepong landslide
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: A 34-year-old Bangladeshi worker was killed after being buried under tonnes of earth in a landslide at Kampung Melayu Kepong here today. Kuala Lumpur Fire and Rescue Department operations commander Mohd Hafizan Hassan said the department received an emergency call at 2.45pm. 4, Jalan 2A/1, Kampung Melayu Kepong.

items.title: Flash floods close Bukit Raja interchange, disrupt traffic on major highways
items.summary: SHAH ALAM: Flash floods following heavy rain this afternoon forced the closure of the Bukit Raja interchange and caused traffic congestion along several major highways in Selangor. "Heavy traffic. Meanwhile, the Malaysian Highway Authority (MHA) reported flash floods at several locations along the Shah Alam Expressway (Kesas).

items.title: SkyeChip, France's SiPearl team up on next-generation computing platform
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: SkyeChip Bhd has signed a non-binding memorandum of understanding (MoU) with France-based SiPearl SAS to jointly develop and commercialise a next-generation computing platform based on Arm Neoverse Compute Subsystems (CSS). The JV would combine SiPearl's expertise in system-level architecture and server central processing units (CPUs) with SkyeChip's silicon intellectual property (IP) portfolio, including high-bandwidth memory interfaces, Network-on-Chip and die-to-die interface IP. SkyeChip said the proposed JV would apply to the relevant Malaysian authorities for an Arm Neoverse CSS licence.

items.title: Trump in Manila for Asean-US talks
items.summary: MANILA: US President Donald Trump arrived in the Philippines this afternoon to attend the 49th Asean Summit and Related Summits, marking his first visit to the country in nine years. Trump subsequently attended the Asean-US Special Summit at the Philippine International Convention Centre (PICC). Trump last visited the Philippines in November 2017 to attend the 31st Asean Summit and Related Summits during his first term as US president.

items.title: Court of Appeal lets Kluang animal group pursue challenge over council’s handling of stray dogs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — The Court of Appeal today granted leave to Kluang Animal Protection Association to commence judicial review seeking a declaration that the Kluang Municipal Council (MPK) had breached the Ministry of Urban Wellbeing, Housing and Local Government Secretary-General’s standard operating procedures (SOPs) in handling stray dogs within its vicinity. A three-man bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, Datuk Amarjeet Singh and Alice Loke Yee Ching granted leave in respect of two remedies sought by the association, namely a certiorari order and declaratory reliefs. Justice Shahnaz also said the association’s judicial review application, filed on May 7 last year, had been submitted within the prescribed time limit.

items.title: Dialog Group posts higher net profit of RM165mil in Q1
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Dialog Group Bhd posted a higher net profit of RM165.07 million in the first quarter ended Sept 30, 2026 (Q1 FY27) compared to RM140.01 million in the same period last year. It said in a Bursa Malaysia filing today that revenue rose to RM787.04 million in Q1 FY27 compared to RM656.99 million previously, driven by strong contributions across its businesses, particularly from its Malaysian operations, reflecting the resilience of its business model and continued execution excellence. "Dialog remains focused on diversifying across the energy sector to navigate economic and oil price cycles, consistent with the group's strategy of generating long-term recurring income," it said.

items.title: Health Ministry to get 1,389 new ambulances after failed supply deal
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The Health Ministry will receive 1,389 new ambulances, following a decision not to renew an earlier supply contract after the appointed company delivered only 115 of the 590 units ordered. Health Minister Datuk Seri Dr Dzulkefly Ahmad said suppliers for 989 ambulances would be finalised next month, while another 400 units had been approved under the 2027 Budget. "The ministry was supposed to receive 590 new ambulances by the end of 2024 at the latest, through a contract awarded in 2022.

items.title: French President Macron departs Malaysia after two-day official visit
items.summary: SEPANG, Nov 17 — French President Emmanuel Macron departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day official visit, which was made at the invitation of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The visit was Macron’s first to Malaysia since he assumed office in May 2017. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion).

items.title: Macron departs Malaysia after two-day official visit
items.summary: SEPANG: French President Emmanuel Macron departed Malaysia today after concluding his two-day official visit, made at the invitation of Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. The visit was Macron's first to Malaysia since he assumed office in May 2017. In 2025, total trade between Malaysia and France amounted to RM17.78 billion (US$4.17 billion).

items.title: Court allows partial challenge over Kluang council's stray dog SOPs
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA: The Court of Appeal today granted leave to the Kluang Animal Protection Association to pursue a judicial review challenging the Kluang Municipal Council's (MPK) handling of stray dogs. A three-member bench comprising Justices Datuk Dr Shahnaz Sulaiman, Datuk Amarjeet Singh and Alice Loke Yee Ching granted leave for two remedies sought by the association: a certiorari order and declaratory reliefs. Shahnaz also said the association's judicial review application, filed on May 7 last year, had been submitted within the prescribed time limit.

items.title: Selangor weighs stricter rules for chicken slaughterhouses, may require certified halal slaughterers
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — The Selangor state government is formulating a stricter policy to improve enforcement and coordination at commercial chicken slaughterhouses, including a proposal requiring licensed premises to employ at least one certified halal slaughterer. State Islamic Religious Affairs and Innovation Culture Committee chairman Mohammad Fahmi Ngah said the move was aimed at ensuring compliance with halal slaughtering standards and maintaining the quality of the state’s food supply. He said 60 slaughterhouses in Selangor were licensed by local authorities (PBT), while another 149 had certified halal slaughterers but no PBT licences.

items.title: BN demands disclosure of KLSCAH land premium assessment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: Barisan Nasional has demanded that the government disclose the formula, valuation basis and approval minutes behind the reduction of the Kuala Lumpur and Selangor Chinese Assembly Hall (KLSCAH) land premium from RM4.67 million to RM1,000. Yeoh said the 103-year-old building was gazetted as a heritage building in 2007. He said the site's original valuation stood at RM4.67 million despite the building's heritage status.

items.title: RM2.7bil Salam project to bolster national digital security: Fahmi
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR: The RM2.7 billion madani Submarine Cable Connection (Salam) project will strengthen the resilience and security of Malaysia's digital network while boosting connectivity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak. Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said the project, implemented by Telekom Malaysia (TM), spans about 5,500km with 10 landing stations. Fahmi said the project uses technology from France-based Alcatel Submarine Networks (ASN), a global leader in the field.

items.title: Malaysia eyes French expertise for power grid
items.summary: Deputy Prime Minister Datuk Seri Fadillah Yusof said Malaysia could leverage France's expertise in energy infrastructure, including cable manufacturing and turbines, to develop local capabilities and strengthen regional connectivity. He said discussions covered opportunities for French investors to establish cable manufacturing facilities in Malaysia. He said Malaysia is also exploring broader cooperation with France across the energy value chain.

items.title: Govt open to proposal to expand scope of Pan Borneo Highway probe, says deputy minister
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — The government supports the proposal to expand the scope of the Public Accounts Committee’s (PAC) investigation into the implementation of the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway project, said Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department (Sabah and Sarawak) Datuk Mustapha Sakmud. He said the government was always open to such proposals, as the findings of the PAC investigation could subsequently be presented in Parliament for collective scrutiny. “The government is open to any necessary proposals, including the PAC’s proposal to conduct an investigation.

items.title: Former deputy minister Mashitah Ibrahim settles defamation suit over claims linking her to Myanmar human trafficking
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A defamation suit filed by former Deputy Minister in the Prime Minister’s Department Datuk Dr Mashitah Ibrahim against a non-governmental organisation (NGO) and two individuals over claims of human trafficking in Myanmar was resolved after all defendants issued an apology at the Shah Alam High Court yesterday. The settlement was reached after the Malaysian International Humanitarian Organisation (MHO), its secretary-general Datuk Hishamuddin Hashim and committee member Azirul Syafiq Sazali, the first to third defendants, agreed to apologise and pay RM100,000 in costs to Mashitah. Mashitah’s lawyer Datuk Akberdin Abdul Kadir confirmed that the consent judgment was recorded before Judicial Commissioner Datuk Anita Harun yesterday.

items.title: Couple charged over unlicensed Dinar Dirham investment scheme
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — A married couple faced charges in the Sessions Court here today with accepting public deposits through an unlicensed Dinar Dirham investment scheme between 2016 and 2017. Datuk Muhd Azrainuddin Zainal, 45, and his wife, Datin Nur Ezdiani Baharoddin, 44, each pleaded not guilty to two charges read separately before Judge Awang Kerisnada Awang Mahmud. They are also accused of committing the same offence at a premises in Lorong Perusahaan Ringan 1, Kawasan Perusahaan Ringan, Sri Gombak, between January and November 2017.

items.title: ‘Students must receive royalties’: DPM Zahid calls for fair share from university innovations
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — Students who assist lecturers in developing innovations, including prototypes with commercial potential, should receive royalties in recognition of their contributions and efforts. “Students must receive royalties. Students must also receive their share because they have worked equally hard,” he said when officiating the Putrajaya Festival of Ideas 2026 here today.

items.title: Malaysia seeks closer Asean-India cooperation against cross-border scams
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 17 — Malaysia has called for stronger Asean-India cooperation in cybersecurity and combating cross-border fraud and scams to build a secure and trusted digital ecosystem, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said. Anwar outlined four priorities; digital connectivity, maritime cooperation, economic resilience and disaster management, as Asean and India advance the implementation of their Plan of Action 2026-2030. Touching on disaster management, Anwar urged stronger cooperation in early warning systems, climate modelling and disaster tracking, including joint activities between India’s National Disaster Management Authority and the Asean Coordinating Centre for Humanitarian Assistance on disaster management (AHA Centre).

items.title: Anwar orders swift aid for next-of-kin of officer killed in crash near Tapah, other injured officers
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim has directed that immediate assistance be provided to the next-of-kin of a police officer who died in an accident involving a Royal Malaysia Police (PDRM) van in Sungkai, Perak, today, as well as to other officers injured in the incident. “My condolences to the family of the late Muhammad Shahrul Aliff Yaacob, a police officer who lost his life in an accident involving a police van in Sungkai, Perak, today. “May his family be granted strength and fortitude in facing this loss, and may the injured police officers have a speedy recovery.

items.title: Officer dies, 10 others injured after police van crashes near Tapah
items.summary: IPOH, Nov 17 — A policeman was killed while 10 others were injured after a police van skidded and crashed into a metal barrier at KM352 of the North-South Expressway southbound, near Tapah, today. Perak police chief Datuk Mohd Alwi Zainal Abidin said the incident occurred at about 11.35am when the Maxus van, driven by a police personnel member and carrying 10 passengers, was travelling from the Perak police contingent headquarters to Melaka. Mohd Alwi said the four seriously injured victims were taken to Slim River Hospital for further treatment, while the six others who sustained minor injuries were sent to Tapah Hospital.

items.title: Struggling with PTPTN arrears? Borrower-Friendly Month makes loan restructuring available with minimum RM1,000 payment
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The National Higher Education Fund Corporation (PTPTN) is offering advisory services and loan restructuring facilities to borrowers through the 2026 PTPTN Borrower-Friendly Month. In a statement today, PTPTN said the initiative, running from November 1 to December 15, allows borrowers to seek advice and arrange loan repayments according to their respective financial means. Borrowers, particularly those with repayment arrears, are encouraged to consult PTPTN under the Education Sustainability Campaign to identify suitable repayment methods.

items.title: Two years after GISBH care home raids, Selangor exco says 124 children linked to group are back in school
items.summary: State Women and Social Welfare Development Committee chairman Anfaal Saari said other rehabilitation initiatives included the NURANI (Nilai Unggul, Rohani dan Akhlak Nadi Insan) Advocacy programme, which involved 65 participants. “From the welfare aspect, 64 families of children who met the eligibility criteria were also provided with appropriate welfare assistance, including general assistance, child assistance, and assistance related to Persons with Disabilities (OKU),” she said. Meanwhile, Anfaal said state JKM had also ordered the closure of 10 premises identified as operating as care centres following inspections of 29 welfare homes linked to GISBH across Selangor.

items.title: Macron gets a taste of KL as Anwar takes him around Petaling Street and Pasar Seni
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim today took President Emmanuel Macron on an informal visit to the area around Petaling Street here, in conjunction with the French leader’s official visit to Malaysia. Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim and French President Emmanuel Macron take a 30-minute stroll around Kuala Lumpur’s iconic Pasar Seni and Petaling Street as part of the French leader’s official visit to Malaysia today. French President Emmanuel Macron is welcomed with a flower garland during a visit to Sri Maha Mariamman Temple near Petaling Street with Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim in Kuala Lumpur, November 17, 2026.

items.title: Floodwaters swamp road leading to Kemuning Toll Plaza (VIDEO)
items.summary: SHAH ALAM, Nov 17 — Heavy rain triggered flash flooding near the Kemuning Toll Plaza this afternoon, leaving a key route towards Klang partially submerged and causing significant traffic congestion. https://www.threads.com/@syarmilakhalip/post/Df1YjXyj_Ru?xmt=AQG0mranE-qdWlDxxpDwYtM1_TkZ152AMQK3YtFGn2QQ4gpma_nW_I6Ckv7gQ1lxfk-1YxM The situation also sparked concern among road users heading home during the evening rush hour, with some claiming nearby access roads had also been affected by rising water levels. The Malaysian Highway Authority (LLM) reported a flash flood incident at KM27.3 westbound near the Kemuning Toll Plaza, adding that traffic was moving slowly because of the conditions.

items.title: Melaka exco to include representatives from all BN and Perikatan parties, says Ab Rauf
items.summary: MELAKA, Nov 17 — The new line-up of the Melaka State Executive Council (Exco) will comprise representatives from all component parties of Barisan Nasional (BN) and Perikatan Nasional (PN), said Chief Minister Datuk Seri Dr Ab Rauf Yusoh. He said the state needed a team with a competitive edge and creative thinking to jointly take Melaka to greater heights. He said the state government would begin implementing 113 initiatives under the six manifesto thrusts offered by BN and PN during the 16th Melaka State Election within the first 100 days after the Exco line-up was appointed.

items.title: Education Ministry allocates over RM13b to tackle dilapidated schools nationwide through 2027
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — The Ministry of Education has allocated over RM13 billion to address the issue of dilapidated schools nationwide through the implementation of school building reconstruction projects between 2023 and 2027, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. Deputy Education Minister Wong Kah Woh said the allocation comprised RM1.7 billion in 2023, RM1.8 billion (2024), RM4.1 billion (2025), RM1.3 billion (2026) and RM4.1 billion for next year. He said the allocation reflected the government’s continued efforts to address the issue of dilapidated schools and ensure that educational facilities remained safe and conducive for learning.

items.title: Malaysia backs petroleum stockpiling for regional energy security, but says it must be voluntary
items.summary: MANILA, Nov 17 — Malaysia recognises the value of petroleum stockpiling in strengthening regional energy resilience, but any arrangement should be voluntary and commercially based, said Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim. Anwar reaffirmed Malaysia’s commitment to ensuring that decarbonisation proceeded alongside economic growth and energy security. “Enhancing cross-border power interconnection is critical to maximising the regional utilisation of renewable energy, optimising grid stability, and fostering sub-regional energy trade,” he said.

items.title: MCMC appoints TM to build RM2.7b undersea cable linking Peninsular Malaysia to Sabah, Sarawak
items.summary: CYBERJAYA, Nov 17 — The Malaysian Communications and Multimedia Commission (MCMC) has appointed TM Technology Services Sdn. Sdn Bhd (TM) as the universal service provider for designing, implementing, and operating the Madani Submarine Cable Connection System (SALAM) worth RM2.7 billion. It said in a statement that the project will be funded through the Universal Service Provision (USP) Fund, which means the SALAM system will enhance communication connection capacity between Peninsular Malaysia, Sabah and Sarawak.

items.title: France, Malaysia strike ‘unique’ rare earth deal as defence ties deepen
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — France and Malaysia agreed today to deepen ties in the lucrative field of rare earth minerals and in defence, with visiting President Emmanuel Macron hailing a “new milestone” in relations. Macron, who is on a two-day whistle-stop tour of the Southeast Asian nation, told a news conference that a joint rare earths project will include “the option for refining in France” — a “unique” agreement, according to Malaysia’s Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim. Macron said the joint project was set for an operational launch early next year.

items.title: Anwar: Malaysia keen to attract more French investment, including in rare earths
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — Malaysia is seeking greater French investment in key sectors, particularly rare earth processing, as the two countries look to deepen economic ties, Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim said on today. Anwar said cooperation in the rare earth sector must be built on trust, stressing Malaysia’s commitment to expanding processing activities in an environmentally safe manner. Anwar said French investment in Malaysia continued to grow, citing aerospace, defence and semiconductors among the sectors offering opportunities for further cooperation.

items.title: Labuan-Sabah Bridge feasibility study complete, findings to go before council next year
items.summary: KUALA LUMPUR, Nov 17 — A feasibility study on the proposed Labuan-Sabah Bridge, which could connect the Federal Territory of Labuan to the Sabah Pan Borneo Highway network, was completed on November 15, with its findings set to be presented to the National Physical Planning Council (MPFN) next year, the Dewan Rakyat was told today. He said the findings would be presented at an MPFN meeting chaired by Prime Minister Datuk Seri Anwar Ibrahim for further consideration of the proposed mega project. Nanta said the project would require coordination among several ministries, including the Economy Ministry, Finance Ministry and Federal Territories Ministry, with the Works Ministry responsible for the technical study.

items.title: Nearly 14,000 deepfake, manipulated content items removed after MCMC requests since 2024
items.summary: Communications Minister Datuk Seri Fahmi Fadzil said MCMC had also investigated 61 cases involving the misuse of artificial intelligence (AI) technology under Section 233 of the Communications and Multimedia Act 1998 (Act 588) between January 1 and October 31 this year, with 10 cases brought to court. The minister said the government viewed the misuse of AI technology seriously, particularly in the creation of deepfakes, identity impersonation and the spread of false information. Fahmi noted that the Online Safety Act 2025 (Act 566) also provided a regulatory framework to address harmful online content, including AI-generated material that falls within the categories covered by the law.

items.title: BN submits new Negeri Sembilan MB candidate for Tuanku Muhriz’s approval
items.summary: PUTRAJAYA, Nov 17 — Barisan Nasional (BN) has submitted a candidate for the post of Negeri Sembilan Menteri Besar to the Yang Dipertuan Besar Tuanku Muhriz Tuanku Munawir for consideration and approval following Datuk Ismail Lasim’s resignation. BN chairman Datuk Seri Dr Ahmad Zahid Hamidi said the candidate’s name was submitted to the palace yesterday. “A letter was sent to the Yang Dipertuan Besar of Negeri Sembilan following the submission of Ismail’s resignation letter to Tuanku.

items.title: Russia and Ukraine trade bridge strikes ahead of Xi-Trump-Putin talks
items.summary: KYIV, Nov 17 — Russia hit two major bridges in Kyiv while Ukraine struck Moscow’s link to annexed Crimea for the second night in a row, officials said Tuesday, ahead of a historic meeting of Chinese, US and Russian leaders. US President Trump said the fighting in Ukraine would be among the topics canvassed in the talks, which come at a time of renewed diplomatic activity to find a path to end almost five years of war. European officials on Monday also joined discussions with Ukrainian and US negotiators on ways to draw Russia into “direct engagement” on ending its invasion, launched in February 2022.

items.title: Umno Negeri Sembilan not informed of Ismail Lasim’s resignation plan, says Jalaluddin
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — Umno Negeri Sembilan was not informed directly by Datuk Ismail Lasim about his intention to resign as Menteri Besar, according to the state party chairman, Datuk Seri Jalaluddin Alias. Speaking after a special meeting at the Umno Negeri Sembilan headquarters today, Jalaluddin said the party only learned of the matter through Umno’s national leadership. He did not personally inform Umno Negeri Sembilan,” Jalaluddin told reporters.

items.title: ‘Don’t make others the scapegoat’: Ismail Lasim’s son questions statement on father’s resignation
items.summary: SEREMBAN, Nov 17 — The son of Negeri Sembilan Mentri Besar Datuk Ismail Lasim has questioned a statement issued by another party concerning his father’s resignation, including whether it was made at the party’s direction. In an Instagram post, Naim Ismail, who uses the account @naimismaill_, appeared to suggest that someone was being made a scapegoat over the matter, Kosmo! Did you personally make that statement?
